chapter: Cincinnati, Buffalo, Russell and Fletcher Henderson
title: Sending for Red Allen in 1929
summary: He wrote Russell recommending Red Allen because the New Orleans trumpeter could not read.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: You and Red had been friends, though, in the band with Louis Armstrong, right?
I sent for Red Allen to come here.
What were the circumstances? Why did you send for him?
I don't know. I just, you know, like I hear people talk about I'd never heard him and I'd never seen him play. We were playing the Saratoga Club.

Louis Russell's band and we had - what was the trumpet player, man from New Orleans, and he couldn't read, so I wrote Red a letter and told Louis Russell that I was ready for Red, so he sent for him. That's when Red came here.
So the trumpet player who couldn't read?
What's his name? But he could play. I can't think of his name.
What did you all have to read?
We had arrangements too, you know.
Yeah. But he couldn't read at all. So we had to let him go, he couldn't keep up with the band.
Where did you learn how to read then?
